name: Control a Useful Range
summary: Make a long-reaching attack miss, then hit its recovery.
description: Make a long-reaching attack miss, then hit its recovery.

pages.title: What a Useful Range Is
pages.text: Every attack has a sweet spot: a distance where YOUR poke reaches but THEIRS falls short. Standing there for free is what players call controlling a useful range - the opponent has to take a risk just to get to you.

pages.title: Whiff Punishing
pages.text: When a poke misses, its recovery frames are a gift. If you are standing just outside its reach, you can step in and hit the opponent while they are still stuck recovering. This is whiff punishing - the backbone of EFZ neutral.

pages.title: The Drill
pages.text: Misaki will keep poking at a fixed rhythm. Find the spot where her poke whiffs in front of you, then punish the miss before she recovers. Too close and you get hit; too far and your punish falls short.

tasks.label: Make the poke miss, then hit its recovery (1 of 3)

feedback.success: That was a whiff punish - you hit before they could act again.
feedback.failure: Wait for the poke to miss, then dash in and hit immediately. Too late means the window closed.

tasks.label: Make the poke miss, then hit its recovery (2 of 3)

feedback.success: Again - the whiffed poke paid for itself.
feedback.failure: Stay just outside the poke's reach, then move in the instant it misses.

tasks.label: Make the poke miss, then hit its recovery (3 of 3)

feedback.success: Three clean punishes - this spacing is your useful range.
feedback.failure: Watch the poke, not the opponent. The moment it whiffs, step in and hit.
